01 · ScopeAR4 · H64 · B2

The full scientific workload stays the same

Model

645,020 parameters

H64 throughout; two decoder processor layers; one layer in each encoder. The model was not made smaller for distribution.

Training

Four autoregressive steps

Two input states; each forecast feeds the next. Gradients pass through the rollout. WMSE + KL, beta 1; CRPS weight 0.

Data

42,348 ocean nodes

8,456 fine + 2,097 coarse mesh nodes. Global batch two at every GPU count; FP32 and identical AdamW settings.

History: 2 states→t + 1→t + 2→t + 3→t + 4

08 · Original → MP 1AR4 · H64 · B2

A faster run is not an isolated halo speedup

Observed

+17.5% throughput

Mean end-to-end: 1,877.7 → 1,599.9 ms. Input improves by 58.5 ms; the model-step interval by 219.3 ms.

Interpretation

One GPU has no remote halo

Input layout, checkpoint policy and execution structure differ. The measured gain belongs to that bundle of changes.

Diagnostic clue

AdamW: 17.95 → 0.63 ms

Same optimizer and parameter count. CPU launch gaps or background work may affect the intervals; trace before attributing a cause.

09 · Two → fourAR4 · H64 · B2

Most of the extra time is inside backward

Two → four: +63.0 ms backward, +11.9 ms forward, +7.2 ms weight sync; input saves 8.0 ms. Net: +78.1 ms per global batch.

10 · InputAR4 · H64 · B2

The old 90% data conclusion does not apply

The earlier AR1 experiment used a different loader policy. Both forecast length and input setup changed; AR4 alone cannot be credited for the lower fraction.

11 · Workers and prefetchAR4 · H64 · B2

Low queue wait does not mean free decoding

What is measured

About 6–9 ms queue wait

Workers can prepare later batches during model execution. This foreground wait excludes much background read/decode service time.

What is missing

5–40 ms input remainder

The outer input timer also spans return/cleanup boundaries. Its remainder is not measured as disk I/O or halo traffic.

Decision

Freeze 8 / prefetch 2 first

Removing only MP2's visible input, holding model intervals fixed, offers about 3.2%. CPU contention could affect model time too.

12 · StabilityAR4 · H64 · B2

The ordering persists across all five blocks

Original E2E p95: 2.549 s; MP1: 1.862 s; MP2: 1.476 s; MP4: 1.563 s. Fifty steps within one job are not fifty independent replications.

13 · Loss evidenceAR4 · H64 · B2

All four measured training curves overlap

This repeated physical-data proxy measures execution, not forecast skill. Zero error is drawn at 10⁻¹² only to make a logarithmic chart possible.

14 · Resource trade-offsAR4 · H64 · B2

Choose wall time, capacity or GPU time explicitly

MP1 minimizes GPU-seconds/sample. MP2 minimizes elapsed training-step time. MP4 minimizes per-device peak memory. GPU-seconds here exclude startup and are not the course billing formula.

15 · Memory caveatAR4 · H64 · B2

Align buffer lifetime before a model-only memory claim

Measured

3.408 → 0.965 GiB/GPU

Original to four GPUs: 71.7% lower peak allocated memory. The capacity benefit is substantial despite limited H64 scaling.

Harness difference

A retained preflight batch

The MP runner keeps its first GPU batch throughout measurement. The original replaces it. One global batch is about 93.1 MiB.

Next reference

Match what stays alive

MP1 is 89.4 MiB above the original peak. The retained batch can influence that gap; do not subtract it and claim a corrected peak.

16 · Partition evidenceAR4 · H64 · B2

Equal grid counts are not equal boundary cost

Halo entries are static remote-sender counts within relations, not measured bytes or latency. Similar elapsed rank times can include waiting for another rank.

18 · Profiling planAR4 · H64 · B2

Measure the two-versus-four critical timeline

First

CPU + CUDA trace per rank

Separate useful kernels, launch gaps, replay, pack/transfer/wait and gradient reduction. Use short traces beside an untraced timing reference.

Then

Bounded compute-only control

Reuse the same prepared batches after stopping loader work. Test whether background decoding changes the model intervals.

Exit condition

Attribute the +78 ms

Choose CPU placement, buffer reuse, fusion or halo overlap only after the dominant contribution is measured.

20 · DecisionAR4 · H64 · B2

Use two GPUs for H64 speed; measure what limits four

Current choice

Two GPUs for wall time

Best observed throughput, preserved loss trajectory and about half the per-device memory. Keep the one-GPU case as the scaling denominator.

Next step

Controls + targeted traces

Establish independent repetitions and align input/checkpoint/buffer policy. Then profile and integrate the team's partitions.

Later

Width, depth and batch sweeps

Vary one factor at a time after attribution. Bigger models characterize a new regime; they do not explain this result.
